book_understanding.teaching_order: A textbook draws the circular flow and lists the product, income and expenditure methods as definitions. Here the video ties off the last lesson (variants, base year), then asks a puzzle: if GDP is a sum of products, why does it give national income? The answer starts from the learner's own pocket (my income, then my family's, then the whole country), states the surprising three-way equality as a claim, and then proves it with an imaginary economy that makes one laptop. Claim before proof, small before big.
book_understanding.breakdown_rule: Scale one everyday act (adding incomes) from a person to a family to a country, then prove the equality with a one-product economy in which every number is small and visible.

talmel_summary: The first minute is text: typed variant lines the voice never reads, then about 36 s of base-year talk over a nearly still frame. From 70 s the picture carries the argument together with the voice: one person grows into a family and then a row of people inside the map, the laptop gets factor arrows and paid/sold arrows, and the same 10,000 lands on each sigma term as it is spoken. The picture leads by 1-3 s when the equation and the laptop enter, which works. Weak: income sources are not labelled, and the family's parts are shown but never spoken.

voice.notes: About 192 words per minute, quick and chatty. First person throughout ('main YouTube se 500 kamata hoon'), which makes the numbers feel personal. The proof is said as question and answer ('kitna hai? vo hai 10,000 rupees'), each total with a short pause before the number. Rupee amounts are read in full ('das hazaar rupees'); the closing identity is said in English as one long 'is equal to' chain.

game_ideas.player_does: Is the entrepreneur of a one-laptop country: rents land, hires workers, borrows capital and pays each factor by dragging coins, then sets the laptop's price and sells it to a buyer.
game_ideas.process_happens: Each payment fills a factor reward (rent, wages, interest, profit) and builds the laptop's cost; when the buyer pays, three meters fill: total income, total product value, total spending.
game_ideas.win: All three meters show the same number.
game_ideas.lose: Setting a price above what was paid out leaves a gap between meters that is labelled 'this extra is also someone's income: profit'; once profit is counted the meters match again.

game_ideas.player_does: Matches each factor of production to its reward: land, labour, capital, entrepreneur with rent, wages, interest, profit.
game_ideas.process_happens: A correct match draws a blue arrow from the factor into the laptop and puts the reward on the income band.
game_ideas.win: All four matched and the laptop is built.
game_ideas.lose: A wrong pair (land with interest) makes that worker or owner walk off, and the laptop stays half built, with the right pair shown.
game_ideas.concept: factors of production and their rewards

game_ideas.player_does: Taps people to add their incomes: first oneself, then family members, then rows of people across the map, keeping a running sum.
game_ideas.process_happens: Each tapped person's income flies into the sum; at country scale the sum becomes the NATIONAL INCOME chip and the equation appears beside it.
game_ideas.win: Reach the country total and predict that the product and spending totals will be the same.
game_ideas.lose: Counting someone outside the border shows the person standing outside the map with a 'not inside the territory' note.
game_ideas.concept: national income as the sum of everyone's income

notes_questions.q: Desho ki GDP compare karne ke liye nominal GDP kyon use hoti hai, real GDP kyon nahi?
Aapki income, parivar ki income aur desh ki national income kaise jodenge?
National income nikalne ke teen tarike kaun se hain, aur teeno ka total barabar kyon aata hai?
Factors of production kaun se hain aur har ek ko kya income milti hai?
Ek laptop wali economy mein income = products = expenditure kaise sabit hota hai? Numbers ke saath.

checks_learned: Items listed on screen should be spoken, or marked as reference only; here four variants are typed but never read.
Every amount in a spoken running sum needs its source label next to it (YouTube, rent, job were spoken but not written).
Every number shown in an addition should be spoken, or the voice should say the parts are on screen (the family addends were silent).
A spoken change over time (base year 2004 to 2012) should appear as a change on screen.
Flag more than about 20 s of speech over an unchanged frame (27-63 s here).
When a claim is stated before its proof, the claim's picture (the equation) must stay visible and each proved value must land on its own term (worked well here; enforce it).

teaching_best.why: Turns the word 'Product' in GDP's name into a puzzle, so the rest of the video answers a question the learner now holds.
My income, then my family's, then the country's: a sum the learner already knows how to do grows into national income.
A one-laptop economy makes the three-way equality checkable with four small numbers.
The same 10,000 lands on spending, products and income one after another, which proves the claim on the picture itself.

teaching_weak.why: Opening lists four GDP variants on screen without saying them; the learner reads while hearing something else.
About 36 s on base years over a still frame; the change from 2004 to 2012 is not drawn.
The income side is re-added for about 20 s with numbers already on screen and nothing new shown.
Profit is set at 4000 (double the others) without a word on why, which may raise a doubt the video does not answer.
